q: The total factory overheads of a plant are Rs 6,00,000 and the total direct labour hours are 1,00,000, giving a single blanket rate of Rs 6 per labour hour. options.A: Rs 20 less

options.C: Rs 20 more
options.D: Rs 60 more

options.A: 1 only

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

options.D: There was no change in the stock of finished goods

options.A: Quality inspection, quality assurance and quality audit
options.B: Prevention, appraisal and failure analysis

options.A: 25 per cent

options.A: Debiting the supplier's personal account and crediting the Stores Ledger Control Account
options.B: Debiting the Stores Ledger Control Account and crediting the General Ledger Adjustment Account
options.C: Debiting the Work-in-Progress Ledger Control Account and crediting the Stores Ledger Control Account
options.D: Making no entry at all, because purchases on credit are recorded only in the financial books

options.A: The reverse of compounding, bringing a sum receivable or payable in the future back to its worth at the present time

options.C: The deduction of a cash discount from the price of an asset when it is purchased
options.D: The writing down of the value of an asset each year by way of depreciation

options.A: 1 year
options.B: 2 years
options.C: 3.33 years
options.D: The outlay is never recovered within the life considered

q: A project is chosen over another simply because its expected (probability-weighted) net present value is the higher of the two, no separate allowance being made for the greater spread of its possible outcomes. The decision rule so applied rests on the assumption that the decision-maker is:

options.A: Risk-averse, preferring a certain sum to a gamble of equal expected value
options.B: Risk-neutral, valuing a gamble at its expected monetary value regardless of its spread
options.C: Risk-seeking, preferring the gamble with the wider spread of outcomes
options.D: Concerned only with the worst outcome that can occur

options.A: The selling price
options.B: The sales volume

options.A: 2 years

options.D: 3 years

q: In the appraisal of a long-lived project in a period of continuing inflation, the depreciation charged on its plant is computed on the historical cost of the plant. One consequence of this for the appraisal is that:

options.B: The tax shield grows in real terms at the rate of inflation
options.C: Inflation has no effect at all on the value of the tax shield

options.B: The Net Present Value of the long-lived project will fall by more, because the discounting bears most heavily on its distant inflows

options.D: The preparation of the maximum possible number of budget statements

q: The sales department proposes a budget of 1,00,000 units, the production department reports a capacity of only 80,000 units and the finance department reports that cash will not support even that level. The role of the budget committee in such a situation is to:

options.A: Accept all the three proposals as they stand and consolidate them
options.B: Reject the budgets of all the three departments for the whole year
options.C: Leave each department to work to its own figures independently
options.D: Examine the conflicting proposals together, reconcile them by phasing, capacity additions, price or credit changes, and settle one coordinated and feasible plan for the enterprise as a whole

q: Besides the budget calendar and the forms to be used, a budget manual also commonly lays down:

options.A: The selling prices to be charged to each individual customer
options.B: The procedure for obtaining proper approval for expenditure not provided for in the budget, or in excess of the amount provided, so that no manager treats the budget as either rigid or freely exceedable
options.C: The names of the suppliers from whom materials must be bought
options.D: The dividend to be declared by the enterprise at the end of the year

q: Budgetary control reports lose most of their value if they are prepared perfectly but reach the managers long after the period to which they relate. This is because:

options.A: Managers are interested only in the reports of the current month
options.B: Reports are required to be filed with the auditors before they are seen by managers
options.C: Control is exercised by acting on deviations, and action can be effective only while the period is still current or recent, so reports should be prompt, even if they are based on reasonably approximate figures
options.D: Late reports are not accepted as evidence in any proceeding

q: Budgeted sales of a product are 68,000 units. The opening stock of finished goods is 8,000 units and the closing stock is to be raised to 12,000 units. Experience shows that 10% of the units started in production are rejected as defective and yield no good output. The number of units to be started in production is:

options.A: 80,000 units
options.B: 72,000 units
options.C: 79,200 units
options.D: 68,000 units

q: The total market demand for a product in the current year is 5,00,000 units and it is expected to grow by 20% in the budget year. The enterprise expects to secure a 20% share of the total market in the budget year and to sell its product at Rs 50 per unit. Its budgeted sales value for the budget year is:

An enterprise budgets to sell 50,000 units at Rs 80 per unit. Sales returns are expected to be 2% of the units sold, and a trade discount of 5% is allowed on the invoice price of the goods actually retained by the customers. The budgeted net sales value is:

The budgeted sales value of an enterprise for a period is Rs 18,00,000. Its budgeted cost of production is Rs 12,00,000, it also buys finished goods for resale for Rs 1,00,000, and its stock of finished goods is valued at Rs 1,80,000 at the commencement of the period and Rs 2,20,000 at the end of the period. Its budgeted gross profit for the period is:

An enterprise purchases materials on terms that 40% of each month's purchases are paid in the month of purchase, a cash discount of 2% being earned on such payments, and the balance is paid in the following month. Its purchases were Rs 4,00,000 in March and are budgeted at Rs 5,00,000 in April. The cash to be paid to creditors in April is:
Under a pledge of goods as security for a bank advance for working capital:

options.A: The goods remain in the godown of the borrower and the bank has no right over them
options.B: The ownership of the goods passes permanently to the bank
options.C: The goods are delivered into the possession of the bank, or of its godown-keeper, as security, the ownership remaining with the borrower, and the goods are released as the advance is repaid
options.D: The bank advances the money only against the personal guarantee of the borrower

q: A floating charge created over the current assets of an enterprise has the distinctive feature that:

options.A: It hovers over a shifting body of assets, such as stock and book debts, and the enterprise remains free to deal with those assets in the ordinary course of business until the charge crystallises into a fixed charge on the happening of a specified event, such as default
options.B: It is a charge that carries a floating rate of interest in every case
options.C: It prevents the enterprise from selling any of its stock until the loan is fully repaid
options.D: It can be created only over the cash balance of the enterprise

q: A customer discounts the bills receivable of his enterprise with his bank and receives the proceeds. Until the bills mature and are honoured, the position is that:

options.A: The bank can never claim anything from the customer in respect of the bills
options.B: The bills cease to be connected with the enterprise in any way
options.C: The enterprise need not disclose anything about the discounted bills in its accounts
options.D: The bank retains recourse to the enterprise, so that if a bill is dishonoured on maturity the bank can recover the amount from the enterprise, the discounted bills being in the nature of a contingent liability until they are met

q: An enterprise is required to keep margin money in a deposit with its bank as a condition of the bank issuing guarantees and letters of credit on its behalf. The effect of this requirement on its working capital is that:

options.A: It reduces the working capital requirement, because the guarantees replace cash in every respect
options.B: A part of its funds stands blocked in the deposit and is not available for meeting its operating needs, so that the working capital it must arrange for its operations is increased to that extent
options.C: It has no effect at all, because margin money is not an asset of the enterprise
options.D: The margin money is treated as a part of the share capital of the enterprise

q: Under a usance bill drawn on 'documents against acceptance' terms in trade finance:

options.A: The shipping documents are handed to the buyer only after he has paid the full amount of the bill in cash
options.B: No bill of exchange is drawn at all in such a transaction
options.C: The shipping documents are released to the buyer when he accepts the bill, that is, undertakes to pay it, and the payment itself is made on the due date at the end of the usance or credit period
options.D: The bank guarantees that the buyer will never default on the bill

q: Under a supplier-finance (reverse factoring) arrangement for working capital:

options.A: The buyer confirms the invoices of its suppliers to a bank or finance platform, the financier pays the suppliers early, and the buyer pays the financier on the original due date, so that the suppliers get prompt payment while the buyer retains its normal credit period
options.B: The suppliers of an enterprise are required to lend money to the enterprise for a year
options.C: The enterprise sells its fixed assets to its suppliers and leases them back
options.D: The bank pays the buyer instead of paying the suppliers of the buyer

q: Interest on a cash credit account for working capital is charged by the bank:

options.A: On the whole of the limit sanctioned, whether it is drawn or not
options.B: Only on the days on which the borrower visits the bank
options.C: At a fixed amount agreed at the time of sanction, regardless of the drawings
options.D: On the amount actually outstanding in the account from day to day, that is, on the daily balances drawn, and not on the sanctioned limit as such

q: Banks periodically arrange a stock audit of a borrower enjoying working capital limits mainly in order to:

options.A: Prepare the annual accounts of the borrower on his behalf
options.B: Verify the existence, quantity, condition and valuation of the stocks charged to the bank and the correctness of the stock statements on the basis of which drawing power is allowed
options.C: Fix the selling prices of the products of the borrower
options.D: Decide the dividend to be paid by the borrower

q: An enterprise follows a restrictive policy in holding current assets, keeping its stock and debtors at a low level in relation to its sales. The expected consequence of this policy is that:

options.A: Its return will necessarily be low and its risk also low
options.B: Its working capital will be the highest in its industry
options.C: Profitability may be higher because less funds remain locked up in current assets, but the risk of stock-outs, interrupted production and lost sales through tight credit is also higher
options.D: It will never face any risk of a shortage of stock

q: A revolving line of credit sanctioned by a bank to an enterprise differs from an ordinary term loan mainly in that:

options.A: Within the sanctioned limit and during the period of the agreement, the enterprise may draw, repay and draw again repeatedly, instead of receiving the whole amount once and repaying it only in fixed instalments
options.B: No interest is charged on the amounts drawn under a line of credit
options.C: A line of credit can be used only for purchasing fixed assets
options.D: The bank can never withdraw a line of credit under any circumstances

q: An enterprise takes a credit insurance cover on its trade receivables. The main protection such a cover gives to its working capital is against:

options.A: A fall in the market price of its finished goods
options.B: Damage to its stock by fire and flood
options.C: Fraud committed by its own employees in the cash office
options.D: Loss arising from the failure or insolvency of its buyers to pay for the goods supplied to them on credit, so that a bad debt does not suddenly drain its working capital

q: A bank has sanctioned a cash credit limit of Rs 10,00,000 to an enterprise. The paid-for stock of the enterprise is Rs 8,00,000, on which a margin of 25% is prescribed, and its book debts outstanding for not more than 90 days are Rs 4,00,000, on which a margin of 40% is prescribed. It also has book debts of Rs 1,00,000 outstanding for more than 90 days, which are not eligible, and stock of Rs 2,00,000 which has not been paid for, which is also not eligible. The maximum amount the enterprise can actually draw is:

An enterprise is considering offering a cash discount of 2% to its credit customers. Its credit sales are Rs 30,00,000 a year and 50% of the customers are expected to avail of the discount. The average receivables will fall from Rs 5,00,000 to Rs 2,50,000, and the cost of capital of the enterprise is 15% per annum. The net effect of the proposal is:

options.A: A net loss of Rs 30,000
options.B: A net gain of Rs 37,500
options.C: A net gain of Rs 7,500
options.D: A net loss of Rs 7,500

q: A bank lends Rs 5,00,000 to an enterprise for one year at 10% per annum, the interest for the year being deducted in advance at the time the loan is granted, so that the enterprise actually receives the balance. The effective rate of interest borne by the enterprise on the funds it actually receives is:

The sales of an enterprise are expected to rise by 25%. At the present level of sales, its current assets are Rs 9,00,000, which include a cash balance of Rs 1,00,000 that will remain unchanged, the other current assets varying in proportion to sales, and its current liabilities are Rs 4,00,000, varying in proportion to sales. The additional working capital it will require is:
